subject: porcupine
title: Porcupine Quills Go In Easy and Come Out 4x Harder

scenes.text: A porcupine quill is built to go in easy and stay in.
A North American porcupine carries about 30,000 of them.
The last four millimetres of each quill are covered in microscopic barbs. They focus force, so it needs far less push to pierce muscle.
But the barbs also anchor it. Pulling one out takes about four times the force.
Scientists tested a patch of barbed quills. It took thirty times more energy to peel off than a barbless patch.
Engineers studied them to design better medical needles and adhesives. Easy in, hard out.
